exercise.name: Weighted Russian Twist
steps: Sit with knees bent, lean back slightly and keep your back straight.
Hold a plate, dumbbell or medicine ball in front of your chest.
Turn your shoulders to bring the weight beside each hip in turn.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated on the floor, knees bent ~90 deg, feet on the floor, trunk leaned back ~40 deg with a straight back, one dumbbell held at the chest. The shoulders turn ~45 deg to one side so the weight comes beside the hip; the hips and legs stay still. Obliques are the target, rectus abdominis holds the lean.

setup.target: Sit on the floor, trunk leaned back about 40-45 deg from upright, back straight (not rounded).
setup.why: ACE V-twist: lean back to about 45 deg, straight back. Library: lean back slightly, back straight. 40 deg is the middle.

setup.target: Knees bent about 90 deg, feet flat on the floor (the easier, safer version; feet lifted is the harder version).
setup.why: ACE V-twist keeps knees ~90 deg; feet on the floor is the textbook beginner form.

setup.target: One dumbbell held in front of the chest with both hands, elbows bent.
setup.tolerance: weight 0.2-0.35 m in front of the chest

movement.measure: turn of the shoulders relative to the pelvis; 0 = square
movement.start: 0 deg (weight in front of the chest)
movement.end: about 45 deg to his right (weight beside the right hip)
movement.path: Shoulders and rib cage turn together; the turn comes from the trunk, not just the arms.
Held; does not sit up or fall back as it turns.
Still: the knees do not sway with the turn.
movement.tolerance: knee 80-100 deg; feet do not slide

movement.path: Arms carry the weight down beside the hip as the trunk turns.

muscles.emg: No study measured the Russian twist itself (searched). Closest: curl-up with twist IO 57.3% MVIC vs 61.7% without twist (Crommert, in S1); standing band torso-twist recorded EO in S3 (values in a figure only).
muscles.role: Turn the rib cage on the pelvis; what the exercise is for (library primary).
muscles.surface: Sides of the waist, from the lower ribs down to the hip bone, angled toward the belly.

muscles.emg: Holds the trunk leaned back against gravity; V-sit hold reaches ~80% MVIC RA (Maeo, in S1).
muscles.role: Holds the lean (anti-extension) while the obliques turn.
muscles.surface: Vertical bands down the front of the belly.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Shoulders slump forward, the trunk is a C instead of a straight lean.
mistakes.why_it_matters: ACE asks for a straight back; slumping loads the spine and takes the lean off the abs.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The weight moves side to side but the chest stays square.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The obliques turn the trunk; arm swinging misses the point.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Curl-up with/without twist IO 57.3/61.7% MVIC; V-sit RA ~80% MVIC.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. V-Twist (ACE Exercise Library).
sources.what_it_gave: Lean back ~45 deg, knees ~90 deg, straight back, rotate shoulders side to side.

sources.citation: Calatayud J, Escriche-Escuder A, Cruz-Montecinos C, et al. 2019. Tolerability and muscle activity of core muscle exercises in chronic low-back pain. Int J Environ Res Public Health 16(19):3509. doi:10.3390/ijerph16193509
sources.what_it_gave: Torso-twist (trunk rotation with hips still) recorded with RA/EO EMG; rotation with legs and hips still.

End: shoulders turned to his right
clip_check.target: 35-60 deg; weight beside the right hip, facing the camera side

clip_check.check: Trunk lean the same in both pictures
Buttocks and feet on the floor
